cues.en: As we've discussed, it can be hard to communicate with a project manager, boss or team mates if you don't have a job.
cues.zh: 正如我們剛才討論，如果還沒有工作，就很難和專案經理、老闆或隊友溝通。

cues.en: And if you've recently learned some skills through an online course and acquired some certificates, it can be tempting to jump straight into the next one and get the next certificate and the next.
cues.zh: 如果你剛透過線上課程學會一些技能、拿到證書，可能會很想馬上上下一門，再拿一張又一張證書。

cues.en: But what are you really chasing?
cues.zh: 但你真正追求的是什麼？

cues.en: Are you after more certificates or more skills?
cues.zh: 你想要更多證書，還是更多技能？

cues.en: Now, a thing you should remember is that no matter how good the course you can assume, the skills you learn there will be commoditized.
cues.zh: 有件事要記得：不論課程多好，都可以假設你在其中學到的技能會變得普及。

cues.en: That means many other people will have gone through the same course, acquire the certificates, same skills as you, and then we'll be looking for similar jobs to what you are.
cues.zh: 也就是說，其他許多人會上過同樣的課，取得同樣的證書、擁有相同技能，然後尋找和你類似的工作。

cues.en: Now let's say Janet posts a job vacancy and receives 673 applicants through an online form.
cues.zh: 假設 Janet 刊登職缺，透過線上表單收到 673 位求職者的申請。

cues.en: You can imagine how hard it is for your resume to stand out.
cues.zh: 你可以想像，要讓履歷脫穎而出有多難。

cues.en: Now, this isn't to say you shouldn't apply through an online form.
cues.zh: 這不是說你不該透過線上表單應徵。

cues.en: But if you are really serious about getting a role somewhere, start the job before you have it.
cues.zh: 但如果你真的很想得到某個職位，就在錄取前先開始做那份工作。

cues.en: How?
cues.zh: 怎麼做？

cues.en: By working on and sharing your own projects which relate to the role you're applying for.
cues.zh: 投入並分享自己的專案，而且要與應徵的職務相關。

cues.en: I call this the Weekend Project Principle.
cues.zh: 我稱之為「週末專案原則」。

cues.en: During the week.
cues.zh: 週間，

cues.en: You're building foundational skills through various courses like the one you're going through now.
cues.zh: 你透過各種課程建立基礎技能，例如你現在上的這門課。

cues.en: But on the weekend you design your own projects, projects in line with the role you're after and work on them.
cues.zh: 週末則自己設計符合目標職務的專案，動手去做。

cues.en: Working on your own projects helps you build specific knowledge.
cues.zh: 做自己的專案，能幫你建立特定領域的知識。

cues.en: They're what compound this type of knowledge that you learn in courses into skill.
cues.zh: 這能讓課程裡學到的這類知識，累積轉化成技能。

cues.en: Skill which can't be taught in courses.
cues.zh: 那是無法只靠課程教會的技能。

cues.en: Let's see it in practice.
cues.zh: 我們來看實際例子。

cues.en: Joe.
cues.zh: Joe

cues.en: And Melissa.
cues.zh: 和 Melissa

cues.en: Apply for a data scientist role to Janet.
cues.zh: 向 Janet 應徵資料科學家的職位。

cues.en: They both make it through the interviews and are now sitting in an interview room with Janet.
cues.zh: 兩人都通過前面的面試，現在坐在面試室裡和 Janet 面談。

cues.en: She looks at both their resumes and notice that they've both done similar courses.
cues.zh: 她看過兩人的履歷，發現他們上過類似的課。

cues.en: This is great.
cues.zh: 這很好。

cues.en: And she asked Joe if he's worked on any of his own projects and he tells her no.
cues.zh: 她問 Joe，有沒有做過自己的專案，他說沒有。

cues.en: He's only had a chance to work on coursework but has plenty of ideas.
cues.zh: 他目前只來得及做課堂作業，但有很多點子。

cues.en: Now she asked Melissa the same question and she pulls out her phone and tells Janet that she's built a small app to help read food labels.
cues.zh: 接著她問 Melissa 同樣的問題。Melissa 拿出手機，告訴 Janet，她做了一個協助閱讀食品標籤的小應用程式。

cues.en: Now, you see, Melissa's daughter can't have gluten and got confused every time she tried to figure out what was in the food she was eating.
cues.zh: 因為 Melissa 的女兒不能吃麩質，每次想弄清楚自己吃的食物含有哪些成分，都會感到困惑。

cues.en: Now the atmosphere is built, isn't perfect, but it helps her daughter figure out what foods she should eat.
cues.zh: Melissa 做的應用程式並不完美，但能幫女兒判斷哪些食物可以吃。

cues.en: Now, I want you to ask yourself, if you were Janet.
cues.zh: 現在請你問自己，如果你是 Janet，

cues.en: Which candidate would you lean towards?
cues.zh: 你會偏向選哪一位？

cues.en: You see, working on your own projects helps you build specific knowledge.
cues.zh: 你看，做自己的專案，能幫你建立特定領域的知識。

cues.en: I can't stress this enough.
cues.zh: 這點怎麼強調都不為過。

cues.en: Your own projects are what?
cues.zh: 自己的專案能做什麼？

cues.en: Compound knowledge into skill.
cues.zh: 讓知識累積轉化成技能。

cues.en: Now, what should you work on?
cues.zh: 那麼，該做什麼專案呢？

cues.en: See, the hard part is you've got unlimited options.
cues.zh: 困難之處是，你有無限多種選擇。

cues.en: But the best part is you've got unlimited options.
cues.zh: 但最棒的地方也是，你有無限多種選擇。

cues.en: One method is to find out the ideal company.
cues.zh: 一種方法是，找出理想的公司，

cues.en: As we said before, you want to work for.
cues.zh: 也就是剛才說的，你想進去工作的公司。

cues.en: And then figure out.
cues.zh: 接著弄清楚，

cues.en: Do your research.
cues.zh: 去做研究，

cues.en: What does a person in that position do day to day?
cues.zh: 那個職位的人每天在做什麼？

cues.en: Find out.
cues.zh: 把它查清楚。

cues.en: And then design your own six week project.
cues.zh: 然後設計自己的六週專案。

cues.en: You might be wondering why six weeks?
cues.zh: 你可能會問，為什麼是六週？

cues.en: Well, the worst case is if it doesn't work out, it's only six weeks.
cues.zh: 因為最壞的情況，就算結果不如預期，也只花了六週。

cues.en: And the best case is you're going to surprise yourself at what you can accomplish in 42 days.
cues.zh: 最好的情況則是，你會驚訝自己能在 42 天內完成多少事。

cues.en: Now, if you're still stuck, you can follow your interests, use this same sort of timeline.
cues.zh: 如果還是沒頭緒，就依照興趣，採用同樣的時程。

cues.en: If you don't have an ideal company you'd like to work for, think of an ideal role you'd like to work for.
cues.zh: 如果沒有理想公司，就想想自己理想的職務。

cues.en: Design it yourself again.
cues.zh: 同樣地，自己設計專案。

cues.en: The worst case is after six weeks, you'll know whether to pursue something you're working on.
cues.zh: 最壞的情況是，六週後你會知道，要不要繼續投入目前的方向。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: I set up another six week project or move on to the next thing.
cues.zh: 再安排另一個六週專案，或者改做下一件事。

cues.en: Now, instead of only having a collection of certificates, you've got a story to tell.
cues.zh: 現在，你擁有的不再只是一疊證書，而是一個可以分享的故事。

cues.en: You've got evidence of you trying to put in what you've learned into practice, exactly what you'll be doing on a job.
cues.zh: 你有證據，證明自己試著把學到的知識付諸實踐，而這正是工作時要做的事。

cues.en: And if you're wondering where the evidence comes from, it comes from you.
cues.zh: 如果你想知道證據從哪裡來，答案就是你自己

cues.en: Documenting your work.
cues.zh: 記錄工作過程。

cues.en: Writing it down.
cues.zh: 把它寫下來。

cues.en: Where?
cues.zh: 寫在哪裡？

cues.en: On your own blog, you might be wondering why a blog?
cues.zh: 寫在自己的部落格。你可能會問，為什麼要寫部落格？

cues.en: I'm not even a writer.
cues.zh: 我又不是作家。

cues.en: We've discussed this before, but it's worth repeating because writing down what you're working on helps solidify your thinking.
cues.zh: 這點之前談過，但值得再說一次：寫下自己正在做的事，能讓思緒更扎實。

cues.en: At the same time as helping others on a similar journey to learn from you what you've done.
cues.zh: 同時也能讓走在類似道路上的人，向你學習你做過的事。

cues.en: What would you like to have known when you were at week one?
cues.zh: 如果回到第一週，你會希望自己早點知道什麼？

cues.en: That's the things you can write about.
cues.zh: 那些就是可以寫的內容。

cues.en: You could start with the post per week detailing how your six week project is going, what you've figured out in week one, what you've figured out in the next week, what you're doing in week three.
cues.zh: 可以先每週發一篇文章，詳述六週專案的進展：第一週弄懂了什麼、下一週弄懂什麼、第三週正在做什麼。

cues.en: Remember what something you'd like to have known sooner?
cues.zh: 記住：有什麼是你希望早點知道的？

cues.en: Probably the best type of post you can write is helping your past self, because if you had a question on something, likelihood someone else will have a similar question.
cues.zh: 最值得寫的文章，大概就是幫助過去的自己。因為你曾有過的問題，別人很可能也會遇到。

cues.en: Now again, remember, your project doesn't have to be perfect.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，你的專案不必完美。

cues.en: None are.
cues.zh: 沒有專案是完美的。

cues.en: And your writing doesn't have to be perfect either.
cues.zh: 文章也不必完美。

cues.en: But by the end of the six weeks, the beautiful thing is you're going to have a series of articles detailing your work, as well as something that you can point at and say, This is what I've done.
cues.zh: 但六週結束時，很棒的是，你會有一系列詳述工作過程的文章，以及可以指著它說「這就是我做的成果」的東西。

cues.en: Now, if you're looking for resources to start a blog, I'll leave some in the resources section.
cues.zh: 如果你想找建立部落格的資源，我會在資源區放一些。

cues.en: But at the moment, dev blog by hash node and fast template by the fast eye team are both free and require almost zero set up to get started.
cues.zh: 在錄製當時，Hashnode 的 Devblog，以及 fast.ai 團隊的 fast_template 都免費，幾乎不用設定就能開始。

cues.en: Otherwise, medium is the next place to get writing and to get sharing your own projects.
cues.zh: 不然，也可以在 Medium 開始寫作，分享自己的專案。

cues.en: You can share your articles on Twitter, LinkedIn, or even if you're tactical enough, send them directly to the person in charge of hiring for the role you're after.
cues.zh: 你可以把文章分享到 Twitter、LinkedIn，或者如果策略得宜，直接寄給你目標職務的招募負責人。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So now we've looked at communicating with your team and starting a job before you have it, designing your own six week projects to build specific knowledge.
cues.zh: 我們已經談過如何與團隊溝通，以及在錄取前先開始工作：設計自己的六週專案，建立特定領域的知識。

cues.en: And one of the best ways to communicate you and share your work is documenting it on your blog.
cues.zh: 溝通與分享工作成果的最佳方式之一，就是把過程記錄在自己的部落格。

cues.en: Let's find out how you might communicate with people outside your team.
cues.zh: 接著看看如何和團隊外的人溝通。

cues.en: The kind of people who might be reading your blog.
cues.zh: 也就是可能會閱讀你部落格的人。
